description: A coalition of European research institutes, bio-labs, and open-source AI developers forms an informal 'Open Bioconsortium' to preemptively publish defensive blueprints for detecting and neutralizing AI-designed pathogens. Motivated by rising bio-uplift concerns and the lack of public-sector readiness, the group uses open models at capability level ~52 to simulate threats and release countermeasures under a 'responsible disclosure plus' model. The initiative gains traction in academic circles but draws scrutiny from intelligence agencies worried about dual use.
